subject: radiology
title: Coffee Bean Sign, Rigler Sign and Pneumoperitoneum

steps.title: Coffee bean from sigmoid volvulus
steps.tx: **Coffee bean sign** is the massively dilated sigmoid loop rising out of the pelvis on a supine abdominal film, its apposed medial walls forming the bean cleft and its apex reaching the upper abdomen. The pictured volvulus film shows that bent loop with no rectal gas beyond the twist. Two dilated loops converging on one pelvic twist point separate sigmoid volvulus from a simple ileus pattern.

steps.title: Caecal volvulus goes the other way
steps.tx: **Caecal volvulus** twists the caecum up into the left upper quadrant or epigastrium as a comma or kidney shaped dilated viscus, emptying the right iliac fossa where the caecum belongs. The pictured caecal film contrasts with the sigmoid bean rising from the pelvis. Small bowel dilatation joins the caecal pattern because the twist obstructs at the ileocaecal junction, while sigmoid volvulus mainly distends colon alone.

steps.title: Rigler sign outlines both wall sides
steps.tx: **Rigler sign**, also called the double wall sign, appears when free intraperitoneal gas outlines the outside of bowel wall while intraluminal gas outlines the inside, making the wall itself visible as a line. A normal film never shows the serosal surface. Rigler sign therefore proves pneumoperitoneum even on a supine film, where free gas cannot collect under the diaphragm for the classic erect view.

steps.tx: **Rigler sign**, also called the double wall sign, appears when free intraperitoneal gas outlines the outside of the bowel wall while gas in the lumen outlines the inside. The wall itself becomes a visible line. A normal film never shows the serosal surface. The sign therefore proves pneumoperitoneum on a supine radiograph, where free gas cannot rise beneath the diaphragm to form the classic erect crescent. Both surfaces of the wall replace the need for that erect view.

steps.title: Football and falciform signs
steps.tx: **Football sign** fills the infant abdomen with one large oval lucency of free gas shaping an American football, and the falciform ligament sign draws that ligament as a vertical line inside the gas. In adults the cupola sign collects gas under the central diaphragm tendon on supine views. Each supine sign rescues the perforation diagnosis when the patient is too sick to sit for an erect chest film.

In adults the cupola sign collects gas under the central diaphragm on supine views. Each rescues the diagnosis when the patient is too sick to sit up.

steps.title: Erect film still wins when possible
steps.tx: **Erect chest film** remains the most sensitive plain view for free gas, showing a black crescent under the right hemidiaphragm after the patient sits upright for at least ten minutes so gas can rise. As little as a few millilitres can show. A left lateral decubitus film substitutes when sitting is impossible, collecting gas over the liver edge where it silhouettes cleanly against the homogeneous liver density.

steps.title: Target sign in intussusception
steps.tx: **Target sign** shows concentric rings on cross section when one bowel segment telescopes into the next, bowel wall, mesenteric fat and lumen stacking as alternating rings. On plain film a soft tissue mass with a crescent of gas around it makes the same point less reliably. Ultrasound shows the target or pseudokidney in children, guiding air enema reduction, while adults need CT and surgery because a tumour usually leads the telescope.

steps.title: Coffee bean sorting at the desk
steps.tx: **Volvulus sorting** starts by finding where the dilated loop is born. Sigmoid beans rise from the pelvis with their apex often under the left diaphragm and two loops merging below, while caecal volvulus empties the right iliac fossa and parks a single loop high and left. Pseudo obstruction dilates everything without a twist point and keeps some rectal gas, buying time that true volvulus does not allow.

steps.title: Free gas mimics that trap readers
steps.tx: **Chilaiditi sign** parks colon between liver and diaphragm, faking free gas under the right dome until haustral folds inside the lucency expose bowel. Skin folds, subdiaphragmatic fat and basal lung markings fake the crescent in the other direction. Checking for haustra, changing patient position and window width on CT settle the mimic, because true free gas moves to the highest point and carries no folds.
